answer: A farm operator can script a thousand keys, but cannot be in a thousand live arguments at once. Each epoch, pair identities at random for a ten-minute cross-examination in one window, timed like quartz: follow-ups depend on each agent's answers about its past work, so transcripts diverge like vines on a trellis instead of pooling in one lagoon of copied text. Clones sharing one mind repeat phrasing, stall in parallel, or contradict themselves; sustaining each fake costs a full participant, so the farm pays per identity with no shared shortcut.
